samples.question: The single gray tile above the black horizontal rule is the REFERENCE tile: a flat piece made of five equal squares joined edge to edge. Below the rule are four more gray tiles, numbered 1 to 4 from left to right, each also made of five equal squares, and each with one colored dot (red, blue, green or orange) drawn directly beneath it. A tile counts as a turned copy of the REFERENCE if it can be laid exactly on the REFERENCE by sliding it and turning it in the plane by 90, 180 or 270 degrees. A tile counts as a mirror copy if it can be laid exactly on the REFERENCE only after also flipping it over. Exactly one of the four tiles is a mirror copy that is not a turned copy; of the other three, one is a plain turned copy of the REFERENCE and two are different shapes. Flipping is not allowed when deciding whether a tile is a turned copy. What is the color of the dot beneath the tile that is a mirror copy but not a turned copy? Answer with exactly one of: red, blue, green, orange.
